key_insight: Constraining LLM weight updates to fixed-rank matrix manifolds enables gradient-free fine-tuning while preserving the update rank throughout training.
engineering_relevance: The approach avoids backpropagation activation storage and keeps pretrained weights frozen, offering a memory-efficient fine-tuning strategy.
method: Project random matrices onto the fixed-rank manifold’s tangent space.
Normalize projected directions to correct scale mismatch in the zeroth-order gradient estimator.
Optimize with Zeroth-order Riemannian Gradient Descent (ZO-RGD) or its smoothed variant, ZO-RGD-S.
evidence_signal: LLM fine-tuning experiments across model families and tasks show competitive performance against strong forward-only baselines, with gains in several settings.
watch_item: Convergence relies on trajectory-regularity conditions, and the abstract does not quantify practical memory or runtime savings.
paper_title: Zeroth-Order Riemannian Optimization on Fixed-Rank Manifolds for LLM Fine-Tuning
